plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray, narrow leaves and dense spikes of fragrant flowers that attract bees and butterflies. It is widely cultivated for essential oils, culinary use, and ornamental borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, with major cultivation in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name Lavandula likely comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large composite flower head made of hundreds of tiny florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and mature plants are valued for seeds, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and the United States
plants.funFact: The spiral patterns in a sunflower head follow Fibonacci numbers, which allows the seeds to pack in as efficiently as possible.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial that rises from muddy water on long stalks, bearing large, fragrant flowers and round, water-repellent leaves. It is culturally important in many Asian traditions and is also grown for edible seeds and rhizomes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to August in temperate Asia)
plants.location: Asia, including India, China, Japan, and Vietnam, and northern Australia; widely grown in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic surface structure that makes them self-cleaning, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect'.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with large, rounded flower heads surrounded by showy bracts. Although its main bloom is in spring, in some years a few flowers can appear into the Southern Hemisphere winter, and related Australian natives such as Banksia flower in July.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in Australia (September to November), with Southern Hemisphere winter flowering in related species like Banksia ericifolia
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, particularly the Sydney region of New South Wales
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name comes from an Aboriginal word meaning 'seen from afar'.
